where to adverb

to what place?

also whither, where are you going?, where?

classical

Plaut. Amph. 341: Quō ambulās tū?
Hor. S. 1.9.62–63: unde venīs et quō tendis?
Traupman 406

quō

adverb, interrogative and relative, of motion towards · Wiktionary

where (to)? whither?

English “where are you going?” asks quō, never ubi. As a relative it answers eō, (to) there.

Other words

  • quōrsum — in what direction? (and) to what end?

    adverb · also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 304: neque unde eam neque quōrsum eam; Hor. S. 2.7.21: quōrsum haec tam pūtida tendant (Lewis & Short) · Wiktionary

    From quō vorsum; also “what is it leading to?”: quōrsum haec?

  • Quō, quaesō? — where to, please?

    also used · classical · Traupman 211 · Wiktionary

Examples

  • Quō ambulās tū?

    Where are you off to?Plaut. Amph. 341

  • unde venīs et quō tendis?

    where have you come from, and where are you heading?Hor. S. 1.9.62–63

  • Quō abīs? manē; manē, inquam: quō abīs?

    Where are you going? Wait; wait, I tell you: where are you going?Ter. Hec. 495–496

  • Abī deambulātum. — Deambulātum quō? — Vah! quasi dēsit locus.

    Go for a walk. — A walk where? — Pah! As if there were nowhere to go.Ter. Haut. 587

  • nesciō hercle, neque unde eam, neque quōrsum eam

    I really don’t know where I’m coming from or where I’m goingTer. Eun. 304

See also where, where from, where are we going?, where are you off to?, there, here.
